title: Grade 4 SOCIAL STUDIES — Premium Revision Paper #16

pages.quiz:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #16
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which direction lies between south and east? (1 mark)
   A. South-west
   B. South-east
   C. North-east
   D. North-west

2. What does the letter E stand for on a compass rose? (1 mark)
   A. Edge
   B. Earth
   C. Equator
   D. East

3. Which of these people is most likely to use a compass? (1 mark)
   A. A tailor
   B. A sailor
   C. A baby
   D. A cook

4. A pupil faces the rising sun in the morning. Which direction is on the pupil's right hand? (1 mark)
   A. West
   B. South
   C. North
   D. East

5. On the county map in the lesson, the neighbour drawn on the right side is in which direction from the county? (1 mark)
   A. North
   B. South
   C. West
   D. East

6. Which valley runs from north to south through Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. The Great Rift Valley
   B. The Tana Valley
   C. The Coast Valley
   D. The Kisumu Valley

7. Why are mountains important for water? (1 mark)
   A. They dry up lakes
   B. They make the land flat
   C. They catch rain and give rise to rivers
   D. They stop all rain

8. What is a physical feature? (1 mark)
   A. A building made by people
   B. A market
   C. A road
   D. A natural feature on the surface of the Earth

9. What is a plain? (1 mark)
   A. A waterfall
   B. A steep mountain
   C. Wide flat land
   D. A lake with salt water

10. Which drink is likely to sell more during the hot season? (1 mark)
   A. Cold drinks
   B. Hot porridge
   C. Hot soup
   D. Hot tea

11. Why do tourists visit historic places? (1 mark)
   A. To cut trees
   B. To buy soap
   C. To plant maize
   D. To learn about the past and enjoy the sights

12. Thimlich Ohinga is found in which county? (1 mark)
   A. Nairobi
   B. Turkana
   C. Migori
   D. Mombasa

13. Which pattern describes houses standing close together around a trading centre? (1 mark)
   A. Linear
   B. Scattered
   C. Empty
   D. Clustered

14. Which pattern describes people living along a road or river in a line? (1 mark)
   A. Circular
   B. Clustered
   C. Linear
   D. Scattered

15. Which pattern describes each family living far from the next on its own land? (1 mark)
   A. Crowded
   B. Linear
   C. Clustered
   D. Scattered

16. What is a festival? (1 mark)
   A. A big celebration
   B. A river
   C. A quiet day
   D. A kind of house

17. Which of these is a Maasai red or blue checked cloth? (1 mark)
   A. Shuka
   B. Kanga
   C. Uniform
   D. Kikoi

18. Which cloth is a printed cloth worn especially at the Kenyan coast? (1 mark)
   A. Suit
   B. Jeans
   C. Kanga
   D. Shuka

19. Which statement about culture is true? (1 mark)
   A. Only one culture is right
   B. Culture never changes
   C. Every community's culture deserves respect
   D. Culture is only about clothes

20. What are values? (1 mark)
   A. Good beliefs that guide our behaviour
   B. Kinds of money
   C. Kinds of food
   D. Types of buildings

21. What does conservation of resources mean? (1 mark)
   A. Ignoring resources
   B. Using resources wisely and protecting them
   C. Wasting resources
   D. Selling everything at once

22. Which resource gives electric power from underground steam at Olkaria? (1 mark)
   A. Oil
   B. Coal
   C. Wind
   D. Geothermal heat

23. How do economic activities help a county government? (1 mark)
   A. They cause drought
   B. They stop roads
   C. They close clinics
   D. Businesses pay taxes and fees

24. Which industry uses milk as raw material? (1 mark)
   A. A dairy
   B. A shoe workshop
   C. A cement plant
   D. A sugar mill

25. Why should every sale be recorded? (1 mark)
   A. So that profit disappears
   B. So that pupils have more homework
   C. So that the project fails
   D. So that money can be checked and accounted for

26. What is personal protective equipment used for? (1 mark)
   A. To hide
   B. To make noise
   C. To protect a person from harm
   D. To slow down work

27. Which of these is a viable project? (1 mark)
   A. One that nobody wants
   B. One that people want, is safe and can earn more than it costs
   C. One that is dangerous
   D. One that costs more than it earns

28. In an essay on good citizenship, what should the beginning say? (1 mark)
   A. A list of foods
   B. A recipe
   C. What a good citizen is
   D. The weather report

29. What does fairness mean? (1 mark)
   A. Favouring rich people
   B. Ignoring people
   C. Treating everyone equally
   D. Favouring friends

30. Two pupils want the same ball. What is a peaceful solution? (1 mark)
   A. Hide it
   B. Break it
   C. Take turns to play with it
   D. Fight for it

31. What is peace? (1 mark)
   A. Calm and harmony where people live safely and respect each other
   B. A loud noise
   C. A kind of food
   D. A game

32. Which of these spoils peace? (1 mark)
   A. Forgiveness
   B. Listening
   C. Fairness
   D. Bullying

33. Which of these is a correct body safety rule? (1 mark)
   A. Anyone can touch them
   B. Say nothing
   C. Keep it a secret if someone does
   D. No one should touch your private parts

34. Which of these is a trusted adult? (1 mark)
   A. A parent or teacher
   B. A stranger you met online
   C. A person who threatens you
   D. A person who gives you sweets in secret

35. Why is early marriage harmful? (1 mark)
   A. It helps children learn
   B. It is fun
   C. It stops education and harms health
   D. It makes children rich

36. What is a suggestion box used for? (1 mark)
   A. Collecting rubbish
   B. Pupils drop ideas and complaints
   C. Storing books
   D. Keeping food

37. In a mock session, what should pupils do first after opening? (1 mark)
   A. Read the last minutes
   B. Leave
   C. Fight
   D. Close the meeting

38. What happens when leaders are dishonest? (1 mark)
   A. Trust is lost and resources are wasted
   B. People are happier
   C. Nothing changes
   D. The community grows faster

39. Which of these tasks belongs to the county government? (1 mark)
   A. National defence
   B. County roads
   C. Immigration
   D. Foreign affairs

40. What is public participation? (1 mark)
   A. Citizens leaving
   B. Citizens breaking laws
   C. Citizens giving their views on plans and the budget
   D. Citizens hiding

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Give two reasons why we need to know the location of our county. (2 marks)

42. In a class election, Maria got 14 votes, Juma got 9 votes and 2 papers were spoilt. How many pupils voted? Who won? Show working. (3 marks)

43. Describe five actions that show good citizenship in school. (5 marks)

44. Give two examples of natural resources. (2 marks)

45. Describe four steps to develop a good quality such as punctuality. (4 marks)

46. Describe four things a school can do to promote child rights. (4 marks)

47. Give three benefits of industries to a county. (3 marks)

48. Write a short motto for a school and say what it means. (3 marks)

49. Describe what people do in the cold season to stay healthy and warm. (4 marks)

50. Explain the meaning of an economic activity and give two examples. (3 marks)

51. Describe how you would show a river, a lake and a mountain on a map with a key. (3 marks)

52. State three qualities of a good citizen in school and give an example for each. (3 marks)

53. Explain two ways of showing appreciation to people who help us. (2 marks)

54. Name two artefacts made by communities in Kenya. (2 marks)

55. Explain how you can find east in the morning without a compass. (2 marks)

56. Explain how the Tana River helps people in Kenya. (3 marks)

57. Name two landforms and two water features. (4 marks)

58. Describe how you would draw a sketch map of your county in five steps. (5 marks)

59. Draw a weather chart for three days: sunny, rainy, cloudy. Add a key. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #16 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — South-east
   South-east is half way between south and east.

2. D — East
   E is the short form of east.

3. B — A sailor
   Sailors use compasses to find direction at sea.

4. B — South
   Facing east, south is on the right hand.

5. D — East
   When north is at the top, the right side is east.

6. A — The Great Rift Valley
   The Great Rift Valley runs through Kenya.

7. C — They catch rain and give rise to rivers
   Mountains catch rain and feed rivers.

8. D — A natural feature on the surface of the Earth
   Physical features such as mountains and rivers are natural.

9. C — Wide flat land
   A plain is a wide, flat area.

10. A — Cold drinks
   People are thirsty and feel hot, so they buy cold drinks.

11. D — To learn about the past and enjoy the sights
   Tourism brings income to the local people.

12. C — Migori
   Thimlich Ohinga is in Migori County.

13. D — Clustered
   Clustered means close together in a group.

14. C — Linear
   Linear means in a line.

15. D — Scattered
   Scattered means spread widely apart.

16. A — A big celebration
   Festivals are big celebrations with songs and dances.

17. A — Shuka
   The shuka is a checked cloth worn by the Maasai.

18. C — Kanga
   The kanga is printed cloth popular on the coast.

19. C — Every community's culture deserves respect
   We must respect all cultures.

20. A — Good beliefs that guide our behaviour
   Values guide how we behave.

21. B — Using resources wisely and protecting them
   Conservation keeps resources for the future.

22. D — Geothermal heat
   Olkaria makes electricity from geothermal steam.

23. D — Businesses pay taxes and fees
   Taxes and fees help pay for services.

24. A — A dairy
   Dairies process milk.

25. D — So that money can be checked and accounted for
   Records show that money was handled honestly.

26. C — To protect a person from harm
   PPE protects the wearer.

27. B — One that people want, is safe and can earn more than it costs
   Viable means it can work.

28. C — What a good citizen is
   The introduction gives the main idea.

29. C — Treating everyone equally
   Fair people give everyone equal treatment.

30. C — Take turns to play with it
   Taking turns is fair.

31. A — Calm and harmony where people live safely and respect each other
   Peace is harmony and safety.

32. D — Bullying
   Bullying hurts and frightens people.

33. D — No one should touch your private parts
   Your body belongs to you.

34. A — A parent or teacher
   Trusted adults protect children.

35. C — It stops education and harms health
   Early marriage harms girls and boys.

36. B — Pupils drop ideas and complaints
   It lets everyone share ideas.

37. A — Read the last minutes
   Minutes remind the group of past decisions.

38. A — Trust is lost and resources are wasted
   Dishonesty harms the community.

39. B — County roads
   County roads belong to the county.

40. C — Citizens giving their views on plans and the budget
   People take part in decisions.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: To plan journeys and to know which counties are next to us. Accept sharing resources.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible reason.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: 25 pupils voted. Maria won.
   Working / marking points: 14 + 9 + 2 = 25. 14 is more than 9, so Maria won. 1 mark for the total, 1 mark for the winner, 1 mark for showing working.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Arrive on time, keep the compound clean, respect teachers, share with others, and report bullying.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each action.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Water and soil. Accept forests, minerals, wildlife or fish.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each example.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose the quality, set a small goal, practise every day, and ask a friend to encourage you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Make posters, sing songs on child protection, set up a suggestion box, and include all children in activities.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each activity.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give jobs, they buy farmers' produce, and they pay taxes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Work hard, be kind. It means pupils should study well and be kind to others.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a short motto, 1 mark for its meaning, 1 mark for showing action.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: They wear warm clothes, eat and drink hot foods, sleep under blankets, and wash their hands to avoid colds and flu.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct action.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: An economic activity is work done to earn income or produce goods and services. Examples are farming and fishing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for each example.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: A wavy blue line for a river, a blue patch for a lake and a brown triangle or brown shading for a mountain, with a key that explains them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct symbol described, up to 3.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty: returning lost items. Respect: greeting teachers. Responsibility: doing class duties.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each quality with example.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: Say thank you and treat their work with respect. Accept helping them in return.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: A kiondo basket and a soapstone carving. Accept clay pots, beaded jewellery or wooden stools.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each artefact.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: Face the direction where the sun rises. That direction is east.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for using the rising sun, 1 mark for naming east.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: It supplies water, its dams produce electric power, and its water is used for irrigation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct use.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Landforms: mountain and valley (or hill, plain, plateau). Water features: lake and river (or waterfall, ocean).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

58. (5 marks)
   Answer: Draw the county outline. Draw the sub-county boundaries. Write the names of the sub-counties. Show the neighbouring counties around the edge. Add a north arrow, a title and a key, then colour it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: Three boxes with a sun, a cloud with rain lines and a plain cloud, and a key that names each symbol.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for correct symbols, 1 mark for the days, 1 mark for the key.
